headline: BoC Holds at 2.25% as Canada Adds 14,000 Jobs in March and February Trade Deficit Widens to $5.7B on Record Imports
executive_summary:
The Bank of Canada's Governing Council held the policy interest rate at 2.25%71 on March 18, 2026, the seventh consecutive decision at this level. The Summary of Governing Council Deliberations published in April stated that the US Supreme Court's February 20 ruling on IEEPA tariffs had "no direct implications for sectoral tariffs on Canadian exports" and that "trade-related risks to Canada remained unchanged."72 The Government of Canada 2-year bond traded at 2.79%75, 54 basis points above the overnight rate. The next Fixed Announcement Date is April 29, 2026.

Statistics Canada's Labour Force Survey recorded +14,000 jobs in March 2026, partially reversing February's -84,000 decline.167 The unemployment rate held at 6.7%, the employment rate at 60.6%, and the participation rate at 64.9%. Average hourly wages grew 4.7% year-over-year, up from 3.9% in February — the fastest pace since October 2024. Canada's merchandise trade deficit widened to -$5.7 billion165 in February, the largest since August 2025, as imports reached an all-time record of $72.1 billion (+8.4% M/M) and exports rose to $66.3 billion (+6.4% M/M). The project database tracks 7,427 projects valued at $1,366.9 billion, of which 1,031 are Under Construction and depend on labour-market capacity, and 48 manufacturing projects ($67.4 billion) are tied to motor vehicles and parts exports that rebounded +24.2% in February after January's -21.2% drop.

Canadian real GDP rose +0.1% in January 2026, a second consecutive monthly increase, with the advance estimate for February at +0.2%.164 Mining, quarrying, oil and gas extraction rose +1.2% M/M and construction +1.1% M/M, while manufacturing contracted -1.4% M/M. Headline CPI ran at +1.8% Y/Y in February, the lowest reading since early 2021, with core measures clustered at 2.3–2.4%.159 Upcoming releases: CMHC Housing Starts (Apr 17), StatCan CPI for March (Apr 20), StatCan GDP by Industry for February (Apr 28), and the BoC Fixed Announcement Date with Monetary Policy Report (Apr 29).

national.analysis:
Statistics Canada reported real GDP by industry rose +0.1% M/M in January 2026, a second consecutive monthly increase, with the advance estimate for February at +0.2%.164 Goods-producing industries expanded +0.2% M/M, services-producing industries were close to flat. Within goods, mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction (NAICS 21) rose +1.2% M/M (oil and gas extraction +1.6%), construction (NAICS 23) +1.1% M/M, and utilities (NAICS 22) +0.6% M/M. Manufacturing (NAICS 31-33) contracted -1.4% M/M and -4.6% Y/Y, the steepest monthly decline in the current cycle. The database tracks 48 manufacturing projects ($67.4B), 423 mining/oil-and-gas projects ($259.7B), and 2,430 construction-linked projects ($226.8B) aligned to these NAICS categories.

The March Labour Force Survey167 recorded employment at +14,000 in March, partially reversing February's -84,000 decline. Unemployment held at 6.7%, the employment rate at 60.6%, and the participation rate at 64.9%. Year-over-year, 87,100 more Canadians were employed than in March 2025. Average hourly wages grew 4.7% Y/Y, up 80 basis points from February's 3.9% — the fastest pace since October 2024 — and runs 290 basis points above headline CPI of 1.8% Y/Y.159 The project database tracks 1,031 projects currently Under Construction that depend on labour-market capacity, across categories led by 217 residential projects ($44.4B) and 2,213 infrastructure projects ($182.4B).

Canada's merchandise trade deficit widened to -$5.7 billion in February, $1.5 billion wider than January's -$4.2B and the largest monthly shortfall since August 2025.165 Imports set an all-time record of $72.1 billion (+8.4% M/M), while exports rose to $66.3 billion (+6.4% M/M) — the highest since March 2025 — with increases in 9 of 11 product sections. Motor vehicles and parts exports rebounded +24.2% M/M after January's -21.2% drop, and metal and non-metallic mineral imports rose +45.6% on gold shipments.146 The database links 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B), 48 manufacturing projects ($67.4B), 362 mining projects ($159.5B), and 90 transport and logistics projects ($35.7B) to these trade flows.

Headline CPI ran at +1.8% Y/Y in February, down 50 basis points from January's 2.3% and the lowest reading since early 2021.159 Core measures converged around the 2% target: CPI-median 2.3%, CPI-trim 2.3%, CPI-common 2.4%. Food inflation decelerated to 5.3% from 7.3%. Headline CPI sits 45 basis points below the BoC's 2.25% overnight rate. CMHC reported housing starts at a seasonally adjusted annualized rate of 250,900 in February, +4.5% M/M from 240,148.109 The March housing starts release is scheduled for April 17, and the March CPI release is scheduled for April 20.

global.analysis:
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported March CPI at +0.9% M/M and +3.3% Y/Y85, the highest annual reading since May 2024, driven by +10.9% energy (gasoline +21.2%). Services ex-energy rose +0.2% M/M and +3.0% Y/Y. March nonfarm payrolls came in at +178,000 versus consensus of +59,000, with February revised to -133,000.86 Unemployment fell to 4.3% from 4.4%, with part of the decline attributable to labour-force exit. Average hourly earnings grew +3.5% Y/Y, the slowest pace since May 2021.

The Federal Reserve held the target federal funds range at 3.50-3.75%129 on March 18. The next FOMC meeting is April 28-29, Chair Powell's final meeting before his term ends in May 2026. The US Supreme Court voided IEEPA tariffs on February 20 in Learning Resources v. Trump.151 Trump replaced them with a 10% global import surcharge; CUSMA-originating goods are exempt. Section 232 tariffs on Canadian steel, aluminum, autos, and softwood lumber remain in force under separate statutory authority. The Fed-BoC policy rate spread of 125-150 basis points keeps CAD near 0.7200. Canadian motor vehicle and parts exports rebounded +24.2% M/M in February after January's -21.2% drop. The Penn Wharton Budget Model projects up to US$175 billion in IEEPA-era tariff refunds.5

global.analysis:
The National Bureau of Statistics of China reported the official Manufacturing PMI at 50.4 in March112, up from 49.0 in February and 49.3 in January — the first expansion reading after two months of contraction and the strongest since March 2025. The production sub-index was 51.4 and new orders 51.6. The Non-Manufacturing PMI was 50.1, up from 49.5. Input and output price sub-indices reached four-year highs on crude oil and non-ferrous metals inputs.1 The People's Bank of China held the 5-year Loan Prime Rate at 2.90%. China's 2025 full-year GDP came in at +5.0%, meeting the official growth target.

China is Canada's second-largest merchandise trading partner, accounting for approximately 5% of Canadian merchandise exports. The return to manufacturing expansion is aligned with Canadian crude, canola, potash, wood products, and seafood shipments. Shipping costs from the Strait of Hormuz closure affect Canadian LNG and commodity routes to Asia. Steel prices rose +6.6% on the week as the PMI recovery was reported (SLX proxy +76.3% Y/Y), while Nutrien (potash proxy) fell -2.8% on the week.41 The database tracks 362 mining projects ($159.5B) and 61 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) linked to China-bound commodity flows.

global.analysis:
The European Central Bank held its three key rates at the March 19 Governing Council meeting122: deposit facility 2.00%, main refinancing operations 2.15%, and marginal lending facility 2.40%. The ECB's March projections raised the headline inflation path to 2.6% average for 2026, 2.0% for 2027, and 2.1% for 2028 — an upward revision attributed to Middle East energy assumptions following the Strait of Hormuz closure.107 Euro area Q4 2025 GDP came in at +0.2% Q/Q, HICP inflation at +1.9% Y/Y (below the 2% target), and unemployment at 5.9%. Germany recorded a second consecutive annual GDP contraction.

The ECB deposit rate of 2.00% sits 25 basis points below the BoC's 2.25% overnight rate. The euro traded toward 1.1460 EUR/USD at end-March. Canada-EU trade operates under the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). Germany's contraction is linked to European demand for Canadian resource exports. The next Governing Council meeting is scheduled for April 30.121

global.analysis:
The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee held Bank Rate at 3.75% unanimously on March 18.76 UK CPI ran at +2.8% Y/Y in February, above the 2% target, with preliminary estimates indicating headline inflation running at 3.0-3.5% over the next two quarters on higher energy prices.20 The Office for National Statistics reported Q4 2025 GDP at +0.1% Q/Q and Q4 unemployment at 5.2%.143 The next MPC decision and Monetary Policy Report are scheduled for April 30, with approximately 90% of polled respondents expecting a hold at 3.75% and 5 expecting a 25 basis point hike.

The BoE-BoC policy rate spread of +150 basis points reflects persistent UK inflation relative to Canada's trajectory (1.8% Y/Y headline CPI in February). Canada-UK trade operates under the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) framework. The UK is a net energy importer, and the Strait of Hormuz closure has raised UK energy import costs via seaborne crude and LNG routing. The Government of Canada 2-year bond trades at 2.79%, 96 basis points below the 3.75% UK Bank Rate.77

The project database tracks 546 Ontario projects ($253.0B total parsed value), led by infrastructure with 199 projects ($150.2B); the top pipeline entries are Highway 413 and Bradford Bypass ($31.0B, Under Construction), the Ontario Line ($27.4B, Under Construction), and GO Expansion ($26.1B, Under Construction)57. 26 Ontario projects sit in the federal Impact Assessment Registry — the largest provincial share — including the New Nuclear at Wesleyville Project and the CAFTA Winona Range upgrades21.

goodsIndustries.name: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing & Hunting
goodsIndustries.analysis:
Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting sector GDP fell 1.4% month-over-month in January 2026, the steepest monthly decline among the 20 NAICS industries, while holding +5.4% year-over-year, the strongest annual reading in the set.174 The U.S. Department of Commerce released preliminary results of the seventh administrative review of anti-dumping and countervailing duty orders on Canadian softwood lumber; BC Minister of Forests Ravi Parmar issued a response statement on April 9, 2026.29 Per NRCan, 66% of Canada's 2024 softwood lumber production was exported, approximately 90% of that to the United States.28

Canadian federal and provincial governments have announced more than C$2.1B in softwood lumber support over the past seven months, including a $1.2B BDC-backed Softwood Lumber Guarantee Program, Quebec's $60M wood-processing working capital top-up (March 2026), and a BC Stumpage Payment Deferral Program effective January 1, 2026.45 The project database tracks 17 agriculture and forestry projects ($5.47B), of which 13 forestry records (~$4.7B) fall within the scope of the U.S. DOC review and the Canadian support package.174 Nutrien (NTR) closed at $102.13, down 2.8% on the week, down 4.5% on the month, and up 56.5% year-over-year, registering against the Saskatchewan and Alberta potash records tracked in commodities.json.14

TC Energy and LNG Canada signed commercial agreements in March 2026 to advance Coastal GasLink Phase 2; capacity would expand from 2.1 Bcf/d to 5 Bcf/d via five new compressor stations, with final investment decision expected late 2026 or early 2027. The Conference Board of Canada Index of Consumer Confidence stood at 47.50 in February, down from 49.30 in January; the March reading has not yet been released.156 Retail sales totaled $70.7 billion in January, +1.1% M/M, with a StatCan advance estimate of +0.9% for February.161 Food inflation decelerated to 5.3% Y/Y in February from 7.3% in January, the largest single-month deceleration on record for that component.159
